substantive_delta: A complete deterministic original-scope membership algorithm for the current-v3 finite convex weak-monotonicity definition, with a conservative O(S^13) bit bound and exact common-loop disjoint-turn certificates for every output failure after input-order success. Its SCC criterion makes branching recurrence require global monotonicity, reduces a simple cycle to two adjacent-level side tests, and treats acyclic components by finite inheritance. The combined scope also decides equivalent Wheeler realizability and constructs a realization on YES using credited standard normalization and automatic convex quotient machinery.
why_nonroutine: The decisive new step is an exact characterization of an existential finite partition of unbounded size, with independent erasing output ranges. Input-order recognition, normalization and automatic closure alone do not decide that property: a cyclic turn can be harmless when all its intervals cross one cut. The two-side simple-cycle equivalence separates that case from disjoint recurrent turns, and the branching argument supplies effective obstruction structure. No inspected prior theorem implies this complete SCC test as an elementary corollary. Standard realization ingredients are not promoted as a separate contribution.
significance: The result settles the immutable open-supported decision question on every promised finite input, including partial transitions and erasure, instead of restricting to a bounded path subclass or a fixed number of pieces. It gives a polynomial decision procedure, a computable obstruction bound, and a constructive semantic realization consequence for the same transducer class. This is substantive structural and algorithmic value in automata theory. No claim of optimal complexity, practical indexing improvement, minimal realization or STOC acceptance is made.
scope_limits: Novelty comparison is bounded by the inspected current primary sources, not universal priority.
No polynomial bound for realizability, optimality or minimization is asserted.
Finite code controls supplement the written proof and are not formal verification.
